text: The Patriots' injury situation has gone from bad to worse ahead of Sunday's trip to Buffalo, with defensive stalwarts Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore both ruled out due to shoulder injuries, forcing Mike Reiss to analyze how New England will patch together replacements for the matchup against Josh Allen and the Bills—a particularly grim development given that offensive lineman Greg Van Roten was just placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, further destabilizing the infrastructure around quarterback Drake Maye, who insists his own right shoulder is fine and that his early-season struggles stem from poor decision-making rather than physical limitations. Meanwhile, the Patriots are welcoming Matt Pryor to their offense as reinforcement, while there's at least some good news on the character front: wide receiver Mack Hollins was named the Week 4 NFLPA Community MVP after hosting a Special Olympics Family Field Day for over 125 athletes and their families. As the Bills look to capitalize on New England's depleted roster and Drake Maye's tendency to turn the ball over, Josh Allen will aim to shake off a recent sloppy performance and make the most of the opportunity.
